no kiosk that needs a keyboard found in the ceiling. mosaic-aware detects and protects active nvidia mosaic configurations. owlette won't blindly rewrite a wall it shouldn't touch. read the display \ -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" scoped keys keys are scoped per-site and per-action. a webhook delivery key cannot restart a machine. idempotency-key required on writes every mutating endpoint ten seconds. runs offline, syncs on reconnect agents monitor and recover locally without the cloud. resync resumes automatically when the connection returns. no inbound ports â outbound 443 only no vpn. no firewall holes. just https to firebase. questions, answered. during beta, yes â both tiers, no credit card, no trial clock. after beta: core is $10/machine/month for monitoring, control, deploy, displays, and cortex on a single site. pro is $50/machine/month (3-machine minimum) and adds the public API, CLI, SDK, webhooks, unlimited sites, and roost â incremental project sync with 1 TB included storage per site. no per-user fees on either. no. owlette is windows-only. your mac is fine â it doesn't need monitoring. it'll let you know when something's wrong. loudly. in the middle of a show. the agent keeps running. it monitors and auto-recovers processes whether or not it can reach the cloud. when the connection returns, it syncs everything it missed. your machines don't need the internet to run. they've been alone before. they know how to survive. no inbound ports, no vpn. agents connect outbound over https (port 443) to google's firebase infrastructure. if your network allows general internet access, it just works. locked-down environments may need to whitelist *.googleapis.com and *.firebaseio.com. cortex is owlette's ai fleet assistant â ask it the questions you ask yourself every day: "which nvidia driver are we running?", "restart the media server on node 3", "what crashed at 3am?" it translates natural language into real commands across your fleet. you bring your own api key (openai, anthropic, or any compatible provider). roost is owlette's project sync. point it at a folder â a TouchDesigner project, a content drop, a build output â and it ships only the bytes that changed to every machine on the site, atomically: a machine gets the whole new version or stays on the old one, never a half-copied mess. every deploy is versioned, so you can roll back to any of the last 50 for up to 30 days. it's part of the pro tier and includes 1 TB of storage per site ($0.05/GB after that). no more zipping a folder and RDP-ing into ten machines at 2am. agents connect over tls, credentials are encrypted on-device using a machine-bound key, and oauth tokens are never logged or stored in plaintext. access is managed through firebase auth with optional passkey and two-factor authentication. yes â owlette is FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 (converts to apache 2.0 two years after each release). the full source is on github. fair warning: it requires firebase, a railway (or equivalent) deployment for the web app, and a willingness to blow past your usage limits at 3am debugging support tickets from your neighbor's camper because your furnace broke and it's -10 outside. we won't talk you out of it, but the hosted version exists for a reason. job.title: Message Center Operator
job.jdText: Amentum is seeking a Message Center Operator to support the Atlantic Undersea Test and Evaluation Center (AUTEC) Mission in Andros Island, Bahamas . AUTEC is a Major Range and Test Facility Base (MRTFB) and the Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Division Newport's largest single team project, providing both deep and shallow water test and training environments. The Message Center Operator is responsible for maintaining strict accountability for Local Element CMS/EKMS and other associated classified materials, records, and equipment in the Communications Message Center. They will also be responsible for receiving, processing, and distributing incoming and outgoing Naval and civilian message traffic for the AUTEC project. Must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S. Government Clearance. Note: U.S. Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance. Responsibilities: Proficiency in loading classified material utilizing electronic devices and adherence to stringent COMSEC procedures. Monitor communications circuits during real-time test operations and initiates action to rectify circuit outages. Monitor all circuits for ACC when ACC is not staffed. Report equipment malfunctions to appropriate technical and management personnel. Maintain and establish radio and telephone communications as required including adherence to proper procedures and record keeping. Maintain a detailed daily official record of tasks/duties/events accomplished or observed in the Communications Message Center. Perform other duties as assigned, required or directed. Qualifications: High school graduate/equivalent or better. 3-5 years related experience working in a communications computer media environment. Military Message Center/EKMS experience desired and preferred. Ability to pass Message Center Communications Qualifications requirements within 60 days of hire. Maintain and sustain training and level of knowledge requirements in associated administrative and limited technical disciplines. Adapt to a rotating shift schedule (12-hour increments). Maintain a consistent high standard of professionalism with customers and coworkers. Able to follow a structured chain of command. Demonstration of consistently excellent customer service skills required. Occasionally lift/pull/push up to and including 40 pounds of office supplies. Frequently exposed to circuit noise and periodic alarms in the Message Center. Knowledgeable in Microsoft Windows 10 or later and MS Outlook. (Skill in Word, PowerPoint, Excel a plus) Consistently demonstrate excellent oral and written communication skills. This position requires the individual to be eligible to obtain a US Government security clearance; US Citizenship is required Must be able to reside in remote location with limited medical facilities. A valid US Passport and Driverâs License is required. job.company: CCDC - The Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre
job.jdText: We curate and distribute the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD) and associated software used by thousands of organizations across the globe for molecular discovery and design. Our mission is to advance structural science for the public benefit. We operate as a not-for-profit company and registered charity. Although independent, we are a University of Cambridge Partner Institute. We offer an excellent benefits package and a competitive salary in a lively and friendly organization of around 100 staff worldwide. Our activities span scientific research, software development, financial, IT systems, commercial, and support. We strive to provide a unified, connected data experience through a FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) inspired platform where users can easily interrogate all structural and property information in the expanding data universe. Data reimagined. We need great people in every team to continue this mission. Please take a look at our open opportunities â we look forward to hearing from you.
